Make the treatment and the target from start dates

Source: R/rollout.R
trop_rollout.Rd

trop_rollout() makes the treatment indicator, the target, and the event time for a panel in long format. Each unit has one start: the first period of the treatment. A unit without a start is never treated. The treatment does not stop after it starts.

Usage

trop_rollout(unit, time, start, anticipation = 0L, window = c(0, Inf))

Arguments

unit, time

Vectors with one value for each row of the panel. A unit must have only one row for each period.

start

A vector with the start of each row, in the units of time. The value must be the same for all rows of a unit. Use NA for a unit that is never treated, or that starts after the last period of the panel. Each other value must be one of the values of time.

anticipation

The number of periods before the start that are treated.

window

Two event times. The target contains the treated cells with an event time from window[1] to window[2]. The default contains all treated periods from the start.

Value

A data frame with one row for each row of the input and these columns: treated (0 or 1), target (TRUE or FALSE), and event_time (the number of periods since the start, or NA for a unit that is never treated).

Details

With anticipation = k, the k periods before the start are also treated. Thus, the fit does not use them as untreated cells. The event time is the number of periods since the true start. Thus, the anticipation periods have the event times -k to -1.

The target contains the treated cells with an event time in window. With the default window, the anticipation periods are not in the target. Thus, they are not in the estimate. With a negative window[1], the anticipation periods in the window are in the target. Use this for placebo estimates of the periods before the start.

Give the columns to trop() with the arguments treatment, target, and event_time. With event_time, trop_effects() and trop_cells() use these event times. Then the groups are correct also when the panel has no row for some periods, or when the anticipation periods start before the panel. Do not give anticipation to these functions, because the event times already count the anticipation periods. If you do not give event_time to trop(), give the same anticipation to trop_effects() and trop_cells().

The periods are the sorted values of time. The event time counts these periods, not the difference of the time values. Thus, a panel with one row for each month gives the event time in months.

See also

trop(), trop_effects(), trop_cells()

Examples

panel <- expand.grid(unit = 1:4, month = 1:6)
starts <- c(3, 5, NA, NA)
panel$start <- starts[panel$unit]
r <- trop_rollout(panel$unit, panel$month, panel$start, anticipation = 1,
                  window = c(0, 1))
cbind(panel, r)[panel$unit == 1, ]
#>    unit month start treated target event_time
#> 1     1     1     3       0  FALSE         -2
#> 5     1     2     3       1  FALSE         -1
#> 9     1     3     3       1   TRUE          0
#> 13    1     4     3       1   TRUE          1
#> 17    1     5     3       1  FALSE          2
#> 21    1     6     3       1  FALSE          3
# Then, for example:
# trop(data, "y", "treated", "unit", "month", target = "target",
#      event_time = "event_time")
